target.name: Orangewood Labs
target.founder: Abhinav Das, Aditya Bhatia, Akash Bansal

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Orangewood Labs is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $5M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public company in the same sector, including adjacent-stage peers such as Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B, Seed).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchored to the $10M total raised proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier for Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $20M. Peer-median analysis across the four same-sector comparables yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B to $2.0B. The substantial gap between these methods reflects the disparity between a capital-based floor and a market-comparable ceiling; peer multiples incorporate revenue traction, IP defensibility, and market momentum—none of which are quantified in the dataset.

The triangulated range is $17M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $860M. The wide spread reflects genuine uncertainty around Orangewood's revenue, unit economics, and competitive positioning relative to the peer set. Resolution of valuation within this range depends on visibility into current ARR, gross margin profile, and customer concentration risk.
